# Atlas Tasker

> The ticketing system for you and your AI agents: terminal tickets, a local web kanban board, and MCP tools, all in one binary.

Atlas Tasker is a free, MIT-licensed, local-first issue tracker for macOS and Linux. Tickets are Markdown files in your repository, every change is an audited event, and humans and coding agents share queues, dependencies, runs, evidence, gates, and handoffs. Lightweight by design: no server, no account, no daemon.

Install with `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/myrrazor/atlas-tasker/main/scripts/install.sh | sh`.

## Guidance for agents
Use this file as a site index, not a full-site corpus. To operate Atlas Tasker on a user's machine, prefer the CLI with `--json` and run `tracker --help` for the current command set; exit codes 0-7 and `error.code` values are stable. Use `tracker mcp serve` when a tool-native MCP connection is available, starting with `--tool-profile read` for inspection or `--tool-profile workflow` for authorized ticket work, and pin `--workspace`. Repository guidance from `tracker integrations install` and MCP client registration are separate steps; OpenClaw installation is repository-local unless its explicit `--global` option is used. CLI mutations resolve `--actor`, then `TRACKER_ACTOR`, then `actor.default`, and fail before writing when identity is missing. Supply reasons for mutations; tracked MCP writes and protected or security-sensitive CLI operations require them. Under `review_gate`, required-reviewer approval moves the ticket to `done` without a second completion call. New schedules must be strictly in the future. Treat `canceled` as its own terminal board column: it does not satisfy dependencies or count as Done. Do not scrape the local web board; it is for humans.
